- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or adjust downward by 2–5% in next 3–5 periods.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; apply a “mean reversion” correction: reduce forecast by 1–3% per period until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to underestimate in early periods when sentiment is volatile; add 0.5–1.5% to first 5–7 periods if sentiment is uncertain or mixed.
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤ 0.33) and price is falling, model often undercorrects; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
